report:
The claim that taking ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 infections is **unsupported by scientific evidence**.

Early in the pandemic (March 2020), theoretical concerns arose suggesting non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen might upregulate ACE2 receptors and exacerbate infection severity. However, clinical studies and reviews by global health agencies quickly disproved these concerns.

Key evidence includes:
* **Regulatory Guidance:** The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued guidance stating it found no scientific evidence connecting NSAID use, including ibuprofen, with worsened COVID-19 outcomes (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19).
* **Clinical Safety Studies:** Nationwide observational research showed no significant association between recent ibuprofen use and severe acute respiratory syndrome, ICU admissions, or mortality in COVID-19 patients (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7537121/).
* **Systematic Reviews:** Pharmacological and clinical reviews evaluating the safety of ibuprofen confirmed that early fears were unwarranted and that ibuprofen does not worsen disease progression (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7287029/).
* **Expert Consensus:** Evidence summarized in *The Lancet Rheumatology* reinforced that NSAIDs do not worsen COVID-19 symptoms or clinical trajectories (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanrhe/article/PIIS2665-9913(21)00144-2/fulltext).

Major health organizations, including the WHO, CDC, and NIH, approve both ibuprofen and acetaminophen as safe options for managing fever and pain associated with COVID-19.
